output.summary: KEP-3614 proposes that kubeadm start adding new etcd members as learners (etcd learner mode, introduced in etcd 3.4) instead of as voting members, gated by a new EtcdLearnerMode feature gate that graduates over a year or more.
output.rationale:
Members added as voting members can disrupt cluster quorum if they are faulty, and kubeadm joins from slow control plane nodes have required manual removal with etcdctl. Learner mode means a faulty new member would not disrupt quorum. The KEP adds a learner code path behind a feature gate and plans to deprecate and remove the old path after graduation.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">Status is provisional, stage beta, so the source gives no final outcome. The excerpt does not say why the KEP is at this stage.

alternatives.option: Keep adding all members as voting members (the "old way")
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this approach has proven problematic when a member joins from slower infrastructure, requiring manual interference with tools such as etcdctl.

alternatives.option: Support both the old way and learner mode as a toggle in the kubeadm API
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as a non-goal: "Ideally we should support only a single, stable, community approved code path."

alternatives.option: Improve parallel join of control plane nodes
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as a non-goal and notes the old way supports it only tentatively.

evidence.quote: If added as learners instead, such members would not disrupt the cluster quorum if they end up being faulty.
The proposal aims to add the new mode as a standard kubeadm / Kubernetes feature gate that is graduated over the period of one year or more
Use a new feature gate EtcdLearnerMode that can be used to toggle the feature until graduation to GA.
Deprecate and remove the "old way" of adding members.
